newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil early coffee crop quality pleasant surprise.
newsitem.headline: Brazil early coffee crop quality pleasant surprise.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 harvest is now underway in almost all the country's key regions with many farmers commenting on the good quality of initial pickings.
"The quality is very good. We're seeing some of the best coffee that I've seen in years," said an agronomist at the cooperative in Lucelia, Sao Paulo state.
Traders also have commented on the quality of the new crop which they say has already been shipped in very small qualities to the U.S. and Europe.
"Many people said before the harvest that the fact there had been up to six flowerings would be a problem with quality but so far that doesn't seem to be the case," one dealer said.
Many agronomists attributed the good quality to a long dry spell which began in some regions in mid-March and which only really has been broken in the last few days.
"Since March 17 and May 17 we've only had 50 millimeters of rain," said Mauricio Miarelli at the cooperative in Franca, north Sao Paulo state.
Independent meteorologists Somar in a regular bulletin commented on the low level of rainfall in the southeast region during April.
In the south, east and north of Sao Paulo, the Cerrado and Zona de Mata regions of Minas Gerais state and in Espirito Santo, rainfall was 25 to 70 millimeters lower than expected.
The outlook for May, June and July is for normal rainfall throughout most of the region and for above average precipitation in the center and west of Minas Gerais.
Farmers are now caught between wanting to see good rains in order to ensure good production prospects for the 1998/99 crop but not in such quantity as to get in the way of the harvest.
"The ideal would really be to have good rains this weekend and then the sun to return early next week," Miarelli said.
The harvest in higher regions such as Franca and Guaxupe in Minas Gerais had only just begun, agronomists said.
In Sao Sebastiao do Paraiso, in Minas Gerais state but just across the border from Franca, the harvest was also just getting going with the cooperative receiving only 400 bags so far.
Quality of the early crop was described by agronomists as "reasonable" but this was expected to improve as the harvest picked up.

In the Cerrado region of Minas Gerais, around 10 percent of the expected crop in Araguari had been brought in while picking was just beginnning in the Patrocinio region, said Aguinaldo Lima, president of the local producers' association Caccer.
In the Carmo de Paranaiba region to the east, the harvest would only start in the middle of next month, he added.
In Sao Paulo, around 10 percent had been brought in around Lucelia in the south while 20-30 percent had been collected in Garca further to the east, officials said.

In Parana, the country's most southern producing region, the harvest in the Londrina/Maringa region was said to be 20-30 percent completed, with farmers starting earlier than usual because of the good prices.
"Normally at this stage we would only see five percent collected," said Carlos Fadoni, agronomist at the Maringa cooperative.
Farmers were this year taking care to pick more carefully to ensure better quality, said an agronomist at the nearby cooperative in Cornelio Procopio.
Most advanced as always was the harvest in Espirito Santo, Brazil's larger producer of robusta coffee.
"We started about 30 days ago and we've almost finished. But that's because there's not much coffee," said an agronomist at the cooperative in Sao Gabriel de Palha.
((-Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
